description: A few square meters of thin, white, spun polypropylene fabric, sold in garden stores as frost cloth.  Spread over a garden bed, it traps the ground's warmth on cold nights and keeps young plants a few degrees above the air temperature, while still letting most of the light through.

One garden soil test: four small capsules of reagent powder and a color chart.  Shake a spoonful of soil with water and a capsule, wait for the color, and read off the nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and pH of a bed.  Each set is used up by one test.

A yellow paperback of weather lore, planting tables and frost dates for New England, with ads for liniment in the back.  Carrying it, you can judge the last spring frost and the first fall frost much better when planting.

description: A stapled pamphlet from the state university's agricultural extension service.  It explains nutrient deficiency symptoms, crop rotation, composting, and how much manure, ash or fertilizer to put on a bed.
